_readme: Regression corpus for false positives. When a highlight is wrong, add the sentence here under mustNotFire (with the rule id that fired), fix the rule's linguisticCondition / contextCondition, and the test in false-positives.test.js keeps it fixed. Each mustNotFire case should have a mustFire companion so a fix cannot silently stop the rule from detecting the real thing. knownLimitations are neutral sentences that are still flagged because the phrase itself is the cue; they are tracked as todo tests.

mustNotFire.text: Mr. Tarriela also rejected claims that Chinese personnel had expelled Philippine vessels or handled the situation.
mustNotFire.note: Reported by the team on a ground.news article, 2026-10-06: 'claims' is a NOUN here ('rejected claims that ...'), not a reporting verb.

mustNotFire.text: He denied the claims that the ship was damaged.
The senator's claims that the bill would pass were wrong.
Officials dismissed false claims that the vote was rigged.
She repeated her claim that the data was accurate.
The report of claims that funds vanished spread quickly.
Spain's Socialists won 20 seats in the regional parliament.
The Democratic Socialists of America endorsed the measure.
The Radicals were a nineteenth-century political faction.
Thug Life was an album by a rapper.
mustNotFire.note: proper name at sentence start (next word also capitalized)

mustNotFire.text: Radical Republicans dominated Congress after the Civil War.
mustNotFire.note: historical group name at sentence start

mustNotFire.text: The Notorious B.I.G. released his debut album in 1994.
Officials broke the vicious cycle of arrests with a new program.
The region faces a brutal heat wave this week, forecasters said.
The film is about a village under siege during the war.
The law shows there is no alternative route through the valley.
Studies show that the vaccine reduces hospital stays, according to the journal.
mustNotFire.note: already attributed to a named source

mustNotFire.text: He supposedly left at noon, according to a neighbor.
Trump called the opposition “radical socialists who hate America,” in a speech.
mustNotFire.note: quoted speech (curly quotes): the source said it, not the outlet

mustNotFire.text: He said "these radicals are dangerous" and left.
Mayor calls plan 'a radical betrayal' of voters
“The radical faction pushed for immediate reform,” she said.
mustNotFire.note: quote of the first sentence in a multi-sentence paragraph

mustFire.text: The senator claimed that the bill would pass easily.
He claims that the report is wrong.
Critics also claimed that the plan failed.
Officials, however, claim that costs fell.
The company has claimed that it acted alone.
A vote for the socialists, for the radicals, for the haters.
Radicals stormed the building and hurt several people.
The radical faction pushed for immediate reform.
The disgraced senator resigned from office.
It was a vicious attack on a defenseless man.
Democracy is under siege, he warned.
He said there is no alternative.
But experts warn such a ban would put pressure on prices.
The deal was allegedly worth millions.
“We will not stop,” she said. The radicals attacked.
The senator blasts the plan as reckless.
The rally chanted “Make America Great Again” at the gate.

knownLimitations.text: Sources say the deal could close next week.
knownLimitations.why: the phrase is the cue; a keyword rule cannot know the sources are credible

knownLimitations.text: The study found that research shows no link between the two.
Everyone knows the bakery on Main Street opens at six.
knownLimitations.why: harmless everyday use of a bandwagon phrase

knownLimitations.text: Most people agree that the museum is worth a visit.
knownLimitations.why: harmless everyday use of a bandwagon phrase

knownLimitations.text: The poster read 'Make America Great Again' in red letters.
knownLimitations.why: the slogan really is present; quoting it neutrally is still a slogan

knownLimitations.text: Local workers will do the job at all costs covered by insurance.
knownLimitations.why: idiomatic 'at all costs' with a different meaning

knownLimitations.text: He wrote that it was the only reason for the delay, according to the memo.
knownLimitations.why: causal claim reported from a source

knownLimitations.text: The word 'propaganda' appears 12 times in the archive catalog.
knownLimitations.why: the word is mentioned, not used as a label

knownLimitations.text: The shocking news was confirmed by the ministry.
knownLimitations.why: evaluative adjective; heuristics cannot tell mild from loaded

knownLimitations.text: She said the results were absurd and called for a recount.
knownLimitations.why: evaluative adjective in a quoted opinion

knownLimitations.text: Fans called the match a massive success for the club.
The company is merely one of three bidders for the contract.
A mere three people attended the 1990 meeting.
